title: Quiet Majesticness
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius will be [music] able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see, black is about to get a new queen, and there doesn't seem to be a way to stop that. The dark square bishop has no way to cover a light square, and the knight seems to be simply too far. Even if we give this check to the black king, after the king moves, the knight is simply badly placed to stop this pawn. But luckily, white does have an incredible resource [music] to save this position. And that starts with the counterintuitive knight c7 check, stepping further away from the pawn, but actually the black king only has two possible squares that it can try to go to. If he goes to d6, now after this check, the knight will be in time to stop the promotion. But of course, the black king can simply go to e5, and now claim that there is no further check from the knight. And now it seems like there is simply no way to stop the promotion, right? Well, not exactly. As it turns out, white is completely winning after the incredibly precise knight to b5. The knight is again threatening to stop the pawn. But of course, black can simply promote. But the idea was to follow up with bishop to b8 check, trying to misplace the black king. Because if the king goes to either one of these two squares, there is actually going to be a knight fork, picking up the queen either like this or like this. So, the only option that black has is to come up to e6. But where is the follow up? The black king and the black queen are just too far apart to get forked by the knight. And since the king is on a light square, the dark square bishop is never going to be able to attack it. But see, the beauty of chess is that the most brutal attacks are not always aggressive. Sometimes, the deadliest of moves are also the quietest ones. And a shiver goes down the spine of the player with the black pieces. As white plays the utterly precise bishop to F4. This move completely cages in the black king and if black is not careful this is going to be a checkmate and if the king tries to run this way, don't forget about the fork. So, black has no other choice but to try and defend the C7 square >> [music] >> that the knight is trying to use to checkmate. But, unfortunately after queen to C2 defending [music] that square, there is going to be knight to D4 with another fork and black will have to resign the game. If you love incredible chess, follow for more.
